questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CronJob usage, PVs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, probes, and NetworkPolicy in a realistic backup workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling from ConfigMap
- PVC mounts and tar packaging
- InitContainer tooling prep
- Secret-based credentials for remote backups
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: installer
              image: busybox
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - apk add --no-cache tar pigz
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: alpine:3.18
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - tar -czf /backup/namespace-$(date +%F-%H%M).tar.gz -C /data .
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: backup
                  mountPath: /backup
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - cat
                    - /tmp/healthy
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 60
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /healthz
                  port: 8080
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: backup
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to extend to remote storage? 
- How to implement retention and idempotent backups?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests partitioned StatefulSet upgrades, PDB, and probes in a real CKAD scenario.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet partitioned RollingUpdate
- PodDisruptionBudget for minimum availability
- readinessProbe and startupProbe usage
- Resource requests/limits in containers

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache
  namespace: prod
spec:
  serviceName: "cache"
  replicas: 3
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cache
        image: myrepo/cache:2.0
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "300m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["bash","-lc","redis-cli PING"]
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        startupProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["bash","-lc","true"]
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
```

```javascript
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: cache-pdb
  namespace: prod
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical security hardening and disruption management capabilities for CKAD-level Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Container SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem for container isolation
- PodSecurityContext: fsGroup for proper file permissions on PVC-mounted volumes
- Kernel capabilities: drop ALL to minimize attack surface
- PodDisruptionBudget: maintain minimum healthy pods during maintenance
- Rollout and rollback procedures for safe deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-gateway
  labels:
    app: api-gateway
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-gateway
    spec:
      securityContext:
        fsGroup: 1001
      containers:
      - name: api-gateway
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - "ALL"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /srv
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/app
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: api-gateway-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: api-gateway-config
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-gateway
```

## Verification & Rollback
```bash
# Verify under load
kubectl exec deployment/api-gateway -- curl http://localhost:8080/health
kubectl top pods -l app=api-gateway
kubectl get pods -l app=api-gateway --watch

# Rollback if needed
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway
kubectl rollout status deployment/api-gateway
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical patching of secret-driven TLS rotation, minimal no-downtime reload, and RBAC-friendly safeguards in CKAD scope. It emphasizes inter-container signaling, probe configuration, and availability during secret rotation.

## Key Concepts
- Secret mounting and readOnly
- InitContainer data preparation
- Sidecar for TLS rotation signaling
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Resource requests/limits
- PodDisruptionBudget
- In-cluster secret rotation verification and rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: fintech
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: cert-init
        image: busybox:stable
        command: ["sh","-c","cp -r /tls/current/* /certs/ && echo ready > /shared/gateway.pid"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /certs
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "250m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      - name: tls-reloader
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh","-c","while true; do inotifywait -e modify,create,attrib /tls/current || true; if [ -f /shared/gateway.pid ]; then kill -USR1 $(cat /shared/gateway.pid); fi; done"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /tls
        - name: shared
          mountPath: /shared
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: gateway-tls
      - name: certs
      - name: shared
        emptyDir: {}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test TLS reload without impacting traffic?
- What are failure scenarios during rotation and how would you mitigate them?

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design production-ready, per-namespace observability data flows—a critical skill for platform engineers and SREs. It tests familiarity with Kubernetes security primitives, resource management, and operational patterns that generic deployments often overlook.

## Key Concepts Tested

- **Per-namespace isolation:** Scoping a Deployment to each namespace ensures data locality and prevents cross-namespace metric contamination.
- **PVC-backed data flow:** Tailing from a PVC provides durability and allows pods to restart without data loss.
- **Security hardening:** NetworkPolicies, Secrets, and resource limits demonstrate a defense-in-depth approach.
- **Operational concerns:** Probes, InitContainers, and sidecars reflect real-world operational complexity.

## Common Pitfalls

Candidates often miss NetworkPolicy egress rules, underconfigure resource limits, or overlook the trade-offs between Pushgateway reliability and simplicity. Strong candidates will proactively discuss alternatives like Prometheus scraping or distributed tracing backends.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests per-namespace scoping, ConfigMap-driven config, and a small policy engine. Exercises InitContainers, Secrets, PVC logging, and network boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace Deployment
- ConfigMap-driven configuration
- Lightweight policy checks (privilege, caps, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
- InitContainer with jq/curl
- Secret-based tokens and PVC-backed logs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy scope

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: namespace-scanner
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: namespace-scanner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: namespace-scanner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-progress curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: scanner
        image: myrepo/namespace-scanner:latest
        env:
        - name: PORTAL_URL
          value: "https://compliance-portal/api/v1/scan"
        - name: TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: compliance-portal-token
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: compliance-logs
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this policy in CI?
- How would you handle retries and idempotence when posting digests?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical drift detection in multiple namespaces, using PVCs, InitContainers and in-cluster API calls.

## Key Concepts

- In cluster tooling with InitContainers, Secrets, and PVCs
- Drift vs validation and how to compare live state
- Namespace scoped RBAC and NetworkPolicy
- Tooling: kubeval, kubectl, client-go in a container

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: drift-detector
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: manifests
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: drift-manifests
      - name: drift
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: drift-reports
      initContainers:
      - name: setup-tools
        image: alpine:3.17
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl kubectl kubeval"]
      containers:
      - name: detector
        image: drift-detector:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: manifests
          mountPath: /manifests
        - name: drift
          mountPath: /drift
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /ready
          port: 8080
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
```

## Follow-up Questions

```yaml

metadata:
  name: testbench
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-curl
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl || true"]
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      containers:
      - name: tester
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD mastery: per-namespace isolation, InitContainer usage, secret/config management, and production-grade guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for model pull from Secret
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for runtime parameters
- Probes and HPA for reliability and scale
- Idempotent DB writes to achieve at-least-once delivery
- NetworkPolicy to enforce namespace boundaries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-image-resize
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-resize
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-model
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "download-model.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: model
              mountPath: /models
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry/ns-image-resize:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: { name: resize-secret }
      volumes:
        - name: model
          emptyDir: {}
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: image-resize
                topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
  ```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor idempotency and retry behavior?
- What changes if Kafka offset management moves to a separate transactional store?
